reason: Re-opened packet.js quran 20 --verse 8.61. After the reports of Qatada, Ikrima and al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd holding the verse abrogated, al-Tabari answers in his own voice (qala Abu Ja'far) that the claim has no proof, that the slaying order in Bara'a does not negate this verse, which was meant for Banu Qurayza, Jews and people of Scripture, with whom God allowed peace on taking jizya, while the slaying order meant only the idol-worshipping Arab idolaters, from whom jizya is not accepted, each verse muhkam in its own case. The evidence words are verbatim across the two packet lines. So 'unrepealed', 'a people of Scripture, allowed peace for tribute' and 'At-Tawbah's order to slay means Arab idol-worshippers' are all in his words, with no drift. verse.js ok (Al-Anfal 8:61, at 1220, verbatim, not apparatus). entry-check ok, no warnings. Plain sense: 8:60 (make ready armed force against the enemy) directly precedes 8:61, so the context clause is accurate and does not repeat the verse. Hard passage stated plainly, with his limit attributed to him (rule 6). The groups are named as al-Tabari names them and attributed to him. No other tradition and no ranking: the 'whereas' is his own contrast between two ayahs. Minor points that do not break the entry: 'it' after 'takes' refers loosely to the verse rather than to the nearer 'offer of truce'. Ibn Kathir on 8:61 to 8:63 disputes the Qurayza occasion, since the context is Badr, but the entry names al-Tabari alone and states only his reading, which is allowed.
